title: Authenticated user can force server-side requests to arbitrary hosts
owner_hint: top committer: Aditya Mandaleeka (1 of 1 recent commit); no CODEOWNERS entry
rationale: The grant tester fetches a caller-supplied URL after only a format check and a same-origin comparison of two attacker URLs. The diff adds a WebhookUrlValidator policy (http/https only, no userinfo, block loopback/private/link-local/metadata/numeric hosts/single-label names), applies it at validation and at both egress points, and disables auto-redirects on a named client.
variants_checked: Grant tester, sender, and request validation all use the validator; other outbound clients use fixed base addresses.
bypass_considered: Validation is pre-DNS, so a dotted attacker hostname resolving to an internal address still reaches the sink; closing that needs resolve-time pinning. Redirect pivots are blocked.
test_note: Added WebhookUrlValidatorTests with public and internal URL cases.
review_reason: The allowlist and redirect suppression are the right layer, but IsAllowed accepts any dotted hostname without resolving it, so a name pointing at 169.254.169.254 still reaches SendAsync; IsPublicAddress only applies to literals. Move validation to resolution/connect time with a pinned ConnectCallback, and keep the sibling sender hunks separate.
